89.name: Ashvamedhika Parva
89.note: Ashva means a horse and medha means a sacrifice. Thus, Ashvamedhika Parva or Ashvamedha Parva is about a horse sacri-fice. In the 78-parva classification, Ashvamedhika Parva is the 74th. In the 700-parva classification, Ashvamedhika Parva is Section 89. In the numbering of the chapters in Ashvamedhika Parva, the first number is a consecutive one, starting with the beginning of the Mahabharata. And the second number, within brackets, is the numbering of the chapter within Ashvamedhika Parva. There is a recital of the Anu-Gita. Krishna leaves for Dvaraka and there is a discourse with Utanka on the way. Yud-hishthira collects riches for the horse sacrifice, this section being named after that. Krishna returns to Hastinapura. Parikshit is born dead, but is revived by Krishna. As the horse travels around, Arjuna fights with the Trigartas, Vajradatta (Bhagadatta�s son), the Saindhavas, Babhruvahana (his son through Chitrangada), Magadha, Shakuni�s son and many others. Yudhishthira�s horse sacrifice is held and there is the incident of the mongoose.
